modules.title: Yield and Yield Spread Measures for Floating-Rate Instruments
modules.explanation: Yield measures summarize return under different reinvestment and holding assumptions, while spreads compare a bond with a benchmark curve. Option-adjusted measures are needed when borrower or issuer choices can change cash-flow timing.

lesson: Yield measures summarize return under different reinvestment and holding assumptions, while spreads compare a bond with a benchmark curve. Option-adjusted measures are needed when borrower or issuer choices can change cash-flow timing.

Fixed-income analysis begins with promised and contingent cash flows, then applies rates appropriate for timing and risk. Price sensitivity also depends on how the curve moves and whether the issuer or borrower can change the cash-flow schedule.
